```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(car)

data <- read_sav("data.sav")

subset <- data |> 
    select(Zage_screening, gender, Zdcog_ti, Zdsom_ti, nfc_group) |> 
    filter(nfc_group %in% c("2", "1")) |> # 2 is no need, 1 is unmet need 
    # but why only filter out these two groups??? oh for the logistic regression this is the response...
    # caption says 395 subset of people but dropping NAs removes a portion (9 people)
    # drop_na() |> 
    mutate(nfc_group = as_factor(nfc_group),
           nfc_group = relevel(nfc_group, ref = "No need"),
           gender = as_factor(gender))

subset$nfc_group
# data |> 
#     select(nfc_group)

a <- glm(nfc_group ~ Zage_screening + gender + Zdcog_ti * Zdsom_ti, family = "binomial", data = subset)

summary(a)

Anova(a, test.statistic = "Wald") # this is what the paper has

# Prefer this
Anova(a, test.statistic = "LR")
```

# 1. Project Identification
The paper we chose is "Is type of depressive symptoms associated with patient-perceived need for professional psychological care in depressed individuals with diabetes?", which is available here:
https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0212304

These explanatory variables are used to predict whether respondents had either "Unmet need" vs. "No need" for psychological help.

# 2. Research Questions / Objectives
1. What questions, if any, in the BDI-II test specifically are associated with the response variable (Unmet need / No need)?
2. Are there any groups associated with the respondents' answers, and what variables do those groups have in common?
3. Can we fit a "better" logistic regression model that accounts for statistically significantly more variability in the response compared to the model in the paper?

# 3. Preliminary Methods Plan
At a base level, since the paper requires logistic regression, the entire class topic on logistic regression will likely be needed. We will also need PCA & Clustering for Question 2 to divide the respondents' responses into groups that we can hopefully visually see. We may also need the regularization section to fit a penalized logistic regression model to see if that is useful.

# 4. Data access confirmation
Data is available to download at: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0212304.s001 which is on the supporting information section of the article.
